subtopics.title: Scarcity, Choice and the Economic Problem

questions.question: Scarcity differs from a shortage because scarcity is:
options: A PERMANENT condition — wants always outrun means, while a shortage ends
A problem of poor countries only

questions.question: Opportunity cost is:
options: The money price of a choice
The value of the NEXT BEST alternative given up — the single best thing, not everything forgone
The total of all alternatives given up
The tax paid on a purchase

questions.question: A point INSIDE the production possibility curve shows:
options: UNDERUTILISATION — unemployed workers and idle capacity, producing less than possible

questions.question: The whole production possibility curve shifts OUTWARD when:
options: Resources grow or technology improves — economic growth drawn in one movement

subtopics.title: The Circular Flow and the National Numbers

questions.question: The three LEAKAGES from the circular flow are:
options: Savings, taxes and imports — money leaving the flow
GDP, GNI and per capita income

questions.question: GDP counts only FINAL goods because:
options: Counting the flour and the bread would DOUBLE-COUNT the flour

questions.question: A foreign-owned mine in Limpopo counts in South Africa's GDP because GDP obeys:
options: The WHERE-rule — production within the borders counts, whoever owns it

questions.question: The limits of GDP include that it misses:
options: Unpaid household work, the informal sector's full extent, income distribution and environmental costs

questions.question: A change in the price of a product causes:
options: A MOVEMENT ALONG the curve — price never shifts the curve of the same product
A shift of the whole demand curve
A shift of the whole supply curve

questions.question: A drought strikes maize. The correct four-step analysis is:
options: Supply shifts LEFT, excess demand at the old price, price bid UP, new equilibrium at higher price and lower quantity
Both curves shift left, quantity unchanged

questions.question: At equilibrium:
options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied — the market cleared, no queue and no pile

questions.question: In a price-quantity table, at a price ABOVE equilibrium you read off:
options: EXCESS SUPPLY — quantity supplied minus quantity demanded in that row

subtopics.title: Markets, Value and the Business Cycle

questions.question: Water is essential yet usually cheap, while diamonds are trivial yet expensive, because value is driven by:
options: UTILITY and SCARCITY together — abundance keeps water's price low despite its usefulness

questions.question: A PERFECT market requires:
options: Many buyers and sellers, identical products, full information and free entry — no single participant sets the price

questions.question: The four phases of the business cycle in order are:
Building plans passed are a LEADING indicator because they:
options: Change BEFORE the economy turns — the headlights showing the road ahead

questions.question: The four-hundred-rand wallet against the six-hundred-rand list illustrates:
options: The economic problem — a PERMANENT gap between unlimited wants and limited means, forcing choice
A bad month that will pass

questions.question: "The price tag behind the price tag" is:
options: The OPPORTUNITY COST — the best alternative the rands would otherwise have done
The total of everything not bought

questions.question: Baking INSIDE the oven's limit — racks standing empty — represents:
options: Workers without work and machines standing still — the country producing less than it could

subtopics.title: The Circle of Money on One Street

questions.question: On the Friday street, the circle of money runs:
options: Firms pay wages to households, households spend at firms, and the wages come back over the counters
Money flows only from shops to workers

questions.question: The street's three TAPS are:
options: Firms INVESTING, GOVERNMENT spending, and EXPORT money arriving

questions.question: The loaf counts in GDP but the flour inside it does not, because:
options: Counting both would count the flour TWICE — only finished goods enter the total

questions.question: GNI differs from GDP by:
options: Following the profits HOME — what our people earn anywhere, minus what foreign owners take out

subtopics.title: The Argument That Sets the Price, and the Economy That Breathes

questions.question: Cold drinks priced at five rand vanish before noon. The queue shows:
options: EXCESS DEMAND — the shortage that pulls the price up toward equilibrium

questions.question: "Price moves you along; everything else moves the curve" means:
options: A price change causes movement ALONG a curve, while cold weather, new sellers or cost changes SHIFT the whole curve

questions.question: "The market found equilibrium without a committee" means:
options: The ARGUMENT between buyers and sellers settles the price where the pile and the queue both disappear

questions.question: Unemployment as an indicator is the rearview mirror because it:
options: CONFIRMS the turn after the economy has already made it — a LAGGING indicator
